title: safety-spline-canary-scheduler-and-shadow-mirroring-controller
creator: Ava Morales
description: Implement a deploy-time policy engine (Safety Spline) that drives phased canary exposures, programmable traffic splits, sampled shadow mirroring, and automatic rollback heuristics. This ticket covers the server-side scheduler, control-plane API surface, basic Console wiring, and the first pass of multi-metric guardrails (latency, error rate, model-quality drift). The goal is a safe, observable, and operator-friendly rollout primitive for model lifecycle staging across hosted and dedicated deployments.
acceptance_criteria: API supports declarative canary objects with step schedule (percentages and durations)
Scheduler executes staged traffic shifts according to Safety Spline ramp profiles and emits events for each step transition
Shadow mirroring can be configured per-route with sampling rate and optional synthetic header injection
Auto-rollback triggers when configured multi-metric thresholds are breached and executes configurable rollback policy (immediate, step-back, or pause)
Console UI shows per-step telemetry (p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, quality regression score) and allows manual pause/abort
End-to-end integration test demonstrating a controlled canary rollout and rollback on injected error spike
design_notes: Safety Spline: a spline-interpolated ramp profile that lets operators specify knots (t0=0%, t1=5% for 30m, t2=20% for 2h, t3=100%) and the scheduler computes smooth intermediate steps to avoid sudden traffic jumps
We combine two guardrail layers: fast-signal hard guards (5xx/error rate, p95 latency) and slow-signal quality checks (evals against golden prompts using feature-store callbacks)
Shadow mirroring implemented as non-blocking async dup of request payload, sampled using reservoir sampling for long-tail correctness analysis

Rollback heuristics: configurable actions (rollback-to-stable, step-back-to-x, pause-and-alert) with cooldown and manual override. Rollback decision is a function of weighted-metric score to avoid flapping on noisy single-metric spikes
Telemetry events: step_started, step_completed, step_failed, rollback_initiated, rollback_completed. All events include snapshot of route, model_version, traffic_percentage, metric_snapshot
Policy expressed as small JSON/YAML DSL (see example below) to keep API compatible with existing canary surface while extending ramp profiles and shadow options
implementation_plan: Week 1: API schema design and prototyping Safety Spline ramp computation; review with PM and Design
Week 2: Scheduler implementation in control plane; implement event emission and simple step executor; unit tests
Week 3: Shadow mirroring plumbing in serving runtime (non-blocking dup) + sampling; integrate with scheduler
Week 4: Guardrail evaluation engine (fast and slow signals) + rollback action executor; integrate with metrics pipeline
Week 5: Console wiring for step timeline and controls; end-to-end tests and runbook updates
Week 6: Canary on staging for two internal routes, simulate failures, iterate
qa_plan: Unit tests for ramp math and knot interpolation (edge cases: very short durations, fractional percentages)
Integration test: synthetic service that increases 5xx when traffic > 30% to validate auto-rollback
Chaos test: network latency injection to verify p95-based guardrail triggers
Smoke: Console renders timeline and manual pause/abort works against staging
Regression: validate existing canary API compatibility for simple step schedules
